text: dsh-minimal-router 是面向 DSH desktop 的工具阶段路由插件。它从工具名识别分组，按阶段提示或限制可用工具，并提供按需收窄、阶段状态、路由活动查看等工具；同包还包含连续错误熔断和缓存探针，可记录请求用量。适合需要管理大量工具、观察缓存用量或在连续工具失败时停止重试的 DSH 用户。无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-minimal-router routes DSH tools by task stage, adding hints or restricting available tools. It offers on-demand narrowing, stage status, activity review, a consecutive-error circuit breaker, and a cache probe. For DSH users managing many tools or tracking cache usage; no API key required.

dsh-minimal-router 的功能「按任务阶段路由」：插件根据工具分组和阶段状态提供尾部路由提示，并可限制当前可见工具。
dsh-minimal-router 的功能「按需收窄工具」：route_use 接收分组和持续轮数，临时保留指定组及基础工具，空分组则恢复。
dsh-minimal-router 的功能「连续错误熔断」：熔断模块跟踪工具调用错误，达到配置阈值后阻止继续调用。
dsh-minimal-router 的功能「请求缓存探针」：探针监听模型流，汇总 token 用量和缓存命中信息，并记录请求数据。

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · How the version requirement is actually evaluated：`package.json` declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.4"`. The real check inside DSH is:

```js
range.trim() !== "" && semver.satisfies(runtimeVersion, range, { includePrerelease: true })
```

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · How the version requirement is actually evaluated：| Fact | Meaning |
|---|---|
| It is a **semver range**, not an exact version | Claims that the version must match exactly are wrong |
| **`includePrerelease: true`** | Prerelease hosts match too; `-rc.N` needs no special handling |
| **An empty string counts as unmet → install is refused** | Never set `engines.dsh` to `""` |

offers `set_version_exemption` for a specific runtime version (at your own risk).

Runtime data (probe history, your `custom_stages.json`) lives in **`~/.dsh/minimal-router/`**, never inside
the package — a real dependency install puts the package in a directory that gets replaced on upgrade.

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Why：DSH sends **every** installed plugin's tool schemas on **every** request. With a few dozen plugins that's 100K+ characters of tool descriptions the model re-reads even when it is just chatting.

This plugin groups tools by name, decides which group the current task needs, and (optionally) **physically removes** the rest from the request — then puts the routing hint on the **tail** of the context instead of the head, so the prefix stays cacheable.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Numbers (same machine, same model, measured with `dsh-cache-probe`)：> **Quality gate**: 277 tests (router 177 + guard 21 + probe 31 + fuzz 12 + instrument 28 +
> install-elsewhere 8), **90.32% line coverage** (3649/4040, Node built-in V8 coverage, zero dependencies),
> plus a repo audit on every push that checks imports, entry points, `files` coverage, `engines.dsh` and
> writable paths. No test framework, no bundler, no linter package — only `node:`.

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Tools you get：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `route_stage(stage, force?)` | Switch stage |
| `route_status()` | Current stage, tag census, guard state, unclaimed groups |
| `route_reset()` | Back to `auto`, releases every restriction |
| `route_init()` | Generate `custom_stages.sample.json` from **your** real tools |
| `route_use(groups, turns?)` | Ad-hoc narrowing without any stage table |
| `route_hint(enabled?)` | Turn the tail hint on/off for this session (A/B) |
| `route_activity(limit?, kind?)` | **What it actually did**: switches, restrictions, denials, blocks |
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Tools you get：**`route_*` and `guard_*` are never blocked.** Escape hatches are a hard rule here.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · "What did it actually do?" — `route_activity`：`route_status` tells you the current state; `route_activity` tells you what happened.

```
route_activity()                       # last 20 events
route_activity({ "kind": "deny" })     # only blocked tool calls
```

Seven kinds: `switch`, `restrict`, `deny`, `block`, `grant`, `reset`, `degrade`.
Stored in `~/.dsh/minimal-router/activity.jsonl`, capped at the last 200 events, so it never grows into another thing to read.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Default stages：| Stage | Allowed groups | Auto-triggered by |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` *(default)* | everything, no trim | — |
| `core` | base tools only | core / general |
| `unity-code` | unity + 13 Unity subsystems | code, script, compile, error, unity |
| `unity-ui` | unity, ui, uikit, uiflow, dialogue, quest | ui, layout, button, panel |
| `art` | art, meshy, image, asset | texture, model, sprite, mesh |
| `audio` | audio | sfx, music, audio |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Default stages：Tags are derived from tool names (`unity_object_create` → `unity`, `mcp__meshy__x` → `meshy`). **Groups no stage claims are always allowed**, so a newly installed plugin is never blocked for being unclassified.

> This table looks Unity/Meshy-heavy because that is what the author works on — not because the plugin only supports game development. Swapping it for Python, data analysis, writing, or video editing takes about a minute; see the next section.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Bring your own domain：**Easiest path: use a bundled preset.**

```text
route_init({ "preset": "python-data" })
```

It writes a ready-to-use `custom_stages.json`; reload the plugin and you are done. Bundled presets:
`python-data`, `web-dev`, `writing`, `qq-chat`.

Calling `route_init` with no arguments is the other path: scan your environment and emit a template to edit.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · The zero-config path: let the model decide what it needs this turn：**No stage table required.** The built-in `route_use` tool narrows the tool set on demand:

```text
route_use({ "groups": ["unity"], "turns": 3 })
```

It keeps the `unity` group plus the base tools, trims everything else, and **restores automatically after
3 turns** — nothing to remember to undo. `route_use({ "groups": [] })` releases immediately.

Where do group names come from? `route_status` → `tagCounts`. They are derived from tool names, so you never
define a workflow up front.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Scope the report to the current session：`cache_probe_report` reports the average over all history by default. To see only this session:

```text
cache_probe_report({ "scope": "session" })
```

It returns `session` (a fingerprint — **the raw session id is never written to disk**), `sessionTotal`, and a
session-scoped `summary`.

> Measured once: `session: "8c144bfe"`, `sessionTotal: 1`, `lastHitRate: 0.0097`. That request happened right
> after a plugin reload, and **0.97% is exactly what one full-price prefix rebuild looks like**.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Verify the hint yourself with `route_hint`：```text
route_hint({ "enabled": false })   # off for THIS session only
route_hint({ "enabled": true })    # on
route_hint()                       # query only
```

Takes effect at runtime, no reload. The hint costs 50–126 tokens per turn (~0.1% of the tool declarations),
so "the hint is expensive" is arithmetically impossible — only its **behavioural** effect is worth testing.

It writes `custom_stages.sample.json` containing:
- `discovered` — every tag in your environment, with counts and whether a stage claims it
- `suggestions` — one ready-to-edit stage per unclaimed tag
- `_readme` — the 5 steps

Rename to `custom_stages.json`, edit, restart the plugin. Merge order is **built-in → `custom_stages.json` → `cordis.patch.yml`**; a malformed file is ignored with a warning, never fatal.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Why not fully automatic?：Because **"never block the wrong tool" outranks "save the most tokens"**.

For any tool group that no stage claims, the only safe default is to **allow it**. Guessing what your brand-new tool does would sometimes guess wrong — and a wrong guess blocks you in the middle of a task, which is far worse than not saving a few thousand tokens.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Why not fully automatic?：`route_init` is the compromise: one scan of *your* tools, one template, about a minute of editing, then routing is automatic forever. It lists every unclaimed group with its tool count, so the decision you are confirming is a small, concrete one.

> One line: it is not lazy. Blind guessing is just more expensive than one minute of confirmation.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · If none of your tools belong to a built-in stage：That is the most common way this plugin "installs but saves nothing, silently": the built-in table claims
`unity`/`ui`/`art`/`meshy`/`image`/`audio`/`asset`, and if your machine has none of those tags, the deny list
is always empty. `route_status` now says so out loud:

```json
"stageTableUnused": true,
"stageTableHint": "内置阶段表认领的标签在你这里一个都不存在……"
```

Two ways out:

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Degradation guard (the important one)：| | in-history | not supported / unknown |
|---|---|---|
| Tail hint | on | **off (empty string)** |
| Physical trim | on | **off** |
| Out-of-stage deny | on | on (touches no prompt) |
| Dead-loop lint | on | on |

A boxed warning is printed **once** per model. Unknown models degrade by default (**fail-safe**).

Custom / proxied models that you have verified:

```yaml
trustedModels: ['my-flash']     # precise
unsafeForce: true               # blanket, at your own risk
```
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Degradation guard (the important one)：Demo it without paying for it: `simulateModel: deepseek-v4-pro`.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Safety gate for huge contexts：Switching stage in a very long session costs a full prefix rebuild. When the last request exceeded `contextGuardThreshold` (default `100000` tokens), `route_stage` is **refused** with an explanation, and requires `force: true` to proceed.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Cost gate: pay it back in how many turns?：Mined from **615 real probe records** (60 prefix changes), the cost profile is **bimodal**:

| Type | Count | Share of context that missed |
|---|---|---|
| Cheap | 35 | **0.2% – 1.2%** |
| Catastrophic | 11 | **98% – 99%** |

And it does not correlate with how much changed: a **98,778-byte** tool-list change cost 708 tokens,
while an **481-byte** change cost **581,830**.

Cheap is luck; expensive is risk. So the estimate assumes the worst case (the whole context at full
price) and computes:

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Coexisting with other plugins：| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Another plugin also decides in `tools/pre-execute` | **Safe.** For tools it allows, this plugin always calls `next()` and never overrides someone else's denial; it only short-circuits when it denies itself |
| Compaction / `/trim` plugins | **Recommended pairing.** Do not switch stage *while* a compaction is running — compaction reuses the prefix, and moving the tool list under it wastes the work |
| Another tool router (loadout-style) | **Do not run both.** Two plugins narrowing the same tool set is unpredictable; disable one |
| A message/QQ gate | Coexists as long as that gate also calls `next()`. If messages stop sending, turn `enforceStage` off first to bisect |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Coexisting with other plugins：In one line: this plugin always errs toward **denying one time fewer** — if it cannot compute, it allows;
if a service is missing, it degrades; on an exception it calls `next()`.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Smarter routing (v1.16)：Three additions, **all zero-request** — no extra model call, no second copy of the context.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Smarter routing (v1.16)：| Feature | Default | What it buys you |
|---|---|---|
| **Semantic scoring** (`lib/intent.js`) | on | Picks a stage even when no keyword matched (`"move that button"` → `unity-ui`) |
| **Dead-tool profile** (`lib/usage.js`) | on | `route_status.toolUsage` tells you which tools were **never called** — i.e. which plugins you can uninstall |
| **Adaptive stage** (`lib/adaptive.js`) | **off** | Learns from the last 20 real calls; proposes a switch only when one group hits ≥6 calls and ≥60% share |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Smarter routing (v1.16)：```yaml
intentRouting: true
intentMinScore: 2.0        # raise to be more conservative
intentMinMargin: 0.25      # must lead the runner-up by 25%
usageTracking: true

Semantic guesses go through the **same gates** as keywords (context guard → cost gate → cooldown), so a wrong guess cannot switch immediately. When unsure it returns `null` and the current stage stays put.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Proactive behaviour (v1.18)：| Feature | Default | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| **Smart trim** (`autoRestrictPolicy`) | on | Only physically trims when the rebuild pays back within `switchPaybackTurns` (default 3). A 500K-token session is told to keep the tools rather than burn 500K to save 26K/turn |
| **Suggestion** | on | When the intent score is *close* but not enough, it does not switch — it appends one line to the tail hint: `Tip: looks like art; if so, route_use(["art"],3).` |
| **Deny recovery** | on | Counts whether the model retries with another tool within 2 minutes after a denial. `route_status.denyRecovery` reports the rate, which tells you if the gate is too strict |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Proactive behaviour (v1.18)：```yaml
autoRestrictPolicy: true   # explicit route_stage is never blocked by this
```

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Why：DSH sends **every** installed plugin's tool schemas on **every** request. With a few dozen plugins that's 100K+ characters of tool descriptions the model re-reads even when it is just chatting.

This plugin groups tools by name, decides which group the current task needs, and (optionally) **physically removes** the rest from the request — then puts the routing hint on the **tail** of the context instead of the head, so the prefix stays cacheable.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Numbers (same machine, same model, measured with `dsh-cache-probe`)：> **Quality gate**: 277 tests (router 177 + guard 21 + probe 31 + fuzz 12 + instrument 28 +
> install-elsewhere 8), **90.32% line coverage** (3649/4040, Node built-in V8 coverage, zero dependencies),
> plus a repo audit on every push that checks imports, entry points, `files` coverage, `engines.dsh` and
> writable paths. No test framework, no bundler, no linter package — only `node:`.

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Tools you get：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `route_stage(stage, force?)` | Switch stage |
| `route_status()` | Current stage, tag census, guard state, unclaimed groups |
| `route_reset()` | Back to `auto`, releases every restriction |
| `route_init()` | Generate `custom_stages.sample.json` from **your** real tools |
| `route_use(groups, turns?)` | Ad-hoc narrowing without any stage table |
| `route_hint(enabled?)` | Turn the tail hint on/off for this session (A/B) |
| `route_activity(limit?, kind?)` | **What it actually did**: switches, restrictions, denials, blocks |
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Tools you get：**`route_*` and `guard_*` are never blocked.** Escape hatches are a hard rule here.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · "What did it actually do?" — `route_activity`：`route_status` tells you the current state; `route_activity` tells you what happened.

```
route_activity()                       # last 20 events
route_activity({ "kind": "deny" })     # only blocked tool calls
```

Seven kinds: `switch`, `restrict`, `deny`, `block`, `grant`, `reset`, `degrade`.
Stored in `~/.dsh/minimal-router/activity.jsonl`, capped at the last 200 events, so it never grows into another thing to read.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Default stages：| Stage | Allowed groups | Auto-triggered by |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` *(default)* | everything, no trim | — |
| `core` | base tools only | core / general |
| `unity-code` | unity + 13 Unity subsystems | code, script, compile, error, unity |
| `unity-ui` | unity, ui, uikit, uiflow, dialogue, quest | ui, layout, button, panel |
| `art` | art, meshy, image, asset | texture, model, sprite, mesh |
| `audio` | audio | sfx, music, audio |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Default stages：Tags are derived from tool names (`unity_object_create` → `unity`, `mcp__meshy__x` → `meshy`). **Groups no stage claims are always allowed**, so a newly installed plugin is never blocked for being unclassified.

> This table looks Unity/Meshy-heavy because that is what the author works on — not because the plugin only supports game development. Swapping it for Python, data analysis, writing, or video editing takes about a minute; see the next section.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Bring your own domain：**Easiest path: use a bundled preset.**

```text
route_init({ "preset": "python-data" })
```

It writes a ready-to-use `custom_stages.json`; reload the plugin and you are done. Bundled presets:
`python-data`, `web-dev`, `writing`, `qq-chat`.

Calling `route_init` with no arguments is the other path: scan your environment and emit a template to edit.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · The zero-config path: let the model decide what it needs this turn：**No stage table required.** The built-in `route_use` tool narrows the tool set on demand:

```text
route_use({ "groups": ["unity"], "turns": 3 })
```

It keeps the `unity` group plus the base tools, trims everything else, and **restores automatically after
3 turns** — nothing to remember to undo. `route_use({ "groups": [] })` releases immediately.

Where do group names come from? `route_status` → `tagCounts`. They are derived from tool names, so you never
define a workflow up front.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Scope the report to the current session：`cache_probe_report` reports the average over all history by default. To see only this session:

```text
cache_probe_report({ "scope": "session" })
```

It returns `session` (a fingerprint — **the raw session id is never written to disk**), `sessionTotal`, and a
session-scoped `summary`.

> Measured once: `session: "8c144bfe"`, `sessionTotal: 1`, `lastHitRate: 0.0097`. That request happened right
> after a plugin reload, and **0.97% is exactly what one full-price prefix rebuild looks like**.
section: Scope the report to the current session

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Verify the hint yourself with `route_hint`：```text
route_hint({ "enabled": false })   # off for THIS session only
route_hint({ "enabled": true })    # on
route_hint()                       # query only
```

Takes effect at runtime, no reload. The hint costs 50–126 tokens per turn (~0.1% of the tool declarations),
so "the hint is expensive" is arithmetically impossible — only its **behavioural** effect is worth testing.

```powershell

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · ask the agent:：route_init
```

It writes `custom_stages.sample.json` containing:
- `discovered` — every tag in your environment, with counts and whether a stage claims it
- `suggestions` — one ready-to-edit stage per unclaimed tag
- `_readme` — the 5 steps

Rename to `custom_stages.json`, edit, restart the plugin. Merge order is **built-in → `custom_stages.json` → `cordis.patch.yml`**; a malformed file is ignored with a warning, never fatal.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Why not fully automatic?：Because **"never block the wrong tool" outranks "save the most tokens"**.

For any tool group that no stage claims, the only safe default is to **allow it**. Guessing what your brand-new tool does would sometimes guess wrong — and a wrong guess blocks you in the middle of a task, which is far worse than not saving a few thousand tokens.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Why not fully automatic?：`route_init` is the compromise: one scan of *your* tools, one template, about a minute of editing, then routing is automatic forever. It lists every unclaimed group with its tool count, so the decision you are confirming is a small, concrete one.

> One line: it is not lazy. Blind guessing is just more expensive than one minute of confirmation.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · If none of your tools belong to a built-in stage：That is the most common way this plugin "installs but saves nothing, silently": the built-in table claims
`unity`/`ui`/`art`/`meshy`/`image`/`audio`/`asset`, and if your machine has none of those tags, the deny list
is always empty. `route_status` now says so out loud:

```json
"stageTableUnused": true,
"stageTableHint": "内置阶段表认领的标签在你这里一个都不存在……"
```

Two ways out:

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Degradation guard (the important one)：| | in-history | not supported / unknown |
|---|---|---|
| Tail hint | on | **off (empty string)** |
| Physical trim | on | **off** |
| Out-of-stage deny | on | on (touches no prompt) |
| Dead-loop lint | on | on |

A boxed warning is printed **once** per model. Unknown models degrade by default (**fail-safe**).

Custom / proxied models that you have verified:

```yaml
trustedModels: ['my-flash']     # precise
unsafeForce: true               # blanket, at your own risk
```
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Degradation guard (the important one)：Demo it without paying for it: `simulateModel: deepseek-v4-pro`.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Safety gate for huge contexts：Switching stage in a very long session costs a full prefix rebuild. When the last request exceeded `contextGuardThreshold` (default `100000` tokens), `route_stage` is **refused** with an explanation, and requires `force: true` to proceed.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Cost gate: pay it back in how many turns?：Mined from **615 real probe records** (60 prefix changes), the cost profile is **bimodal**:

| Type | Count | Share of context that missed |
|---|---|---|
| Cheap | 35 | **0.2% – 1.2%** |
| Catastrophic | 11 | **98% – 99%** |

And it does not correlate with how much changed: a **98,778-byte** tool-list change cost 708 tokens,
while an **481-byte** change cost **581,830**.

Cheap is luck; expensive is risk. So the estimate assumes the worst case (the whole context at full
price) and computes:

text:
@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Coexisting with other plugins：| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Another plugin also decides in `tools/pre-execute` | **Safe.** For tools it allows, this plugin always calls `next()` and never overrides someone else's denial; it only short-circuits when it denies itself |
| Compaction / `/trim` plugins | **Recommended pairing.** Do not switch stage *while* a compaction is running — compaction reuses the prefix, and moving the tool list under it wastes the work |
| Another tool router (loadout-style) | **Do not run both.** Two plugins narrowing the same tool set is unpredictable; disable one |
| A message/QQ gate | Coexists as long as that gate also calls `next()`. If messages stop sending, turn `enforceStage` off first to bisect |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Coexisting with other plugins：In one line: this plugin always errs toward **denying one time fewer** — if it cannot compute, it allows;
if a service is missing, it degrades; on an exception it calls `next()`.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Smarter routing (v1.16)：Three additions, **all zero-request** — no extra model call, no second copy of the context.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Smarter routing (v1.16)：| Feature | Default | What it buys you |
|---|---|---|
| **Semantic scoring** (`lib/intent.js`) | on | Picks a stage even when no keyword matched (`"move that button"` → `unity-ui`) |
| **Dead-tool profile** (`lib/usage.js`) | on | `route_status.toolUsage` tells you which tools were **never called** — i.e. which plugins you can uninstall |
| **Adaptive stage** (`lib/adaptive.js`) | **off** | Learns from the last 20 real calls; proposes a switch only when one group hits ≥6 calls and ≥60% share |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Smarter routing (v1.16)：```yaml
intentRouting: true
intentMinScore: 2.0        # raise to be more conservative
intentMinMargin: 0.25      # must lead the runner-up by 25%
usageTracking: true

Semantic guesses go through the **same gates** as keywords (context guard → cost gate → cooldown), so a wrong guess cannot switch immediately. When unsure it returns `null` and the current stage stays put.

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Proactive behaviour (v1.18)：| Feature | Default | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| **Smart trim** (`autoRestrictPolicy`) | on | Only physically trims when the rebuild pays back within `switchPaybackTurns` (default 3). A 500K-token session is told to keep the tools rather than burn 500K to save 26K/turn |
| **Suggestion** | on | When the intent score is *close* but not enough, it does not switch — it appends one line to the tail hint: `Tip: looks like art; if so, route_use(["art"],3).` |
| **Deny recovery** | on | Counts whether the model retries with another tool within 2 minutes after a denial. `route_status.denyRecovery` reports the rate, which tells you if the gate is too strict |

@local/dsh-minimal-router README · Proactive behaviour (v1.18)：```yaml
autoRestrictPolicy: true   # explicit route_stage is never blocked by this
```
